input.prompt:
Fetch the Google Sheet at fileId "REDACTED" (title "2026 CYC Community Sailing Center Participants") using mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__read_file_content. It will likely be too large to return inline — if so, it'll save to a local file described as JSON {fileContent: string}; probe structure with jq first (type/length/keys), then extract/read the full content with jq/python rather than trying to Read() it with offset/limit.

Context: this is the spreadsheet currently built by an automated Clubspot sync job (packages/admin-functions/src/*.ts in this repo — CampsReport, ParticipantsReport, RegistrationsReport, SessionsReport, ContactReport). I already know from reading that code that ParticipantsReport's columns are: Registration Id, Participant Id, Session Join Id, First Name, Last Name, Camp, Class, Session, Session Start, Status, Registration Date, Date of Birth, Gender, Email, Mobile, Postal Code, First Guardian (+ Email + Mobile), Second Guardian (+ Email + Mobile), Emergency Contact (+ Mobile), Medical Details, Allergies, Medication, Last Tetanus Shot. A "Camps" tab has: Camp Id, Category, Name, Start Date, Open, Registration Link, Entry List (note: "Category" is a real column in the live data, e.g. "Adult Sailing", "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Open Boating", "Adventure Sailing" — this wasn't in the CampsReport code as I last read it, so either the code changed or category is derived/appended some other way — worth noting if you can tell from the data).

I'm designing a Directus schema (a "people hub" CRM) to replace/extend this spreadsheet, and need to know:

1. What tabs exist in the workbook (list them all), and for each tab that looks like actual sync output (not a pivot/summary/manual tab), the exact header row.
2. For the main Participants tab specifically: confirm the exact headers match what I described above, note any drift (added/removed/renamed columns), and grab 3-5 sample rows so I can see real data shape (especially: do the same person's name/email appear identically across multiple rows for different registrations, or does the same participant have slightly different contact info in different rows — i.e. evidence of the "same person, data drifted across registrations over time" problem).
3. Is there any tab or column that already tracks *change history* — e.g. a "last updated" timestamp, a status-change log, an audit tab, or anything indicating when a row's data last changed? Or is every tab a flat point-in-time snapshot that gets fully overwritten/rebuilt each sync run?
4. Does "Category" appear as a real column in the Camps tab data? If so what are all the distinct category values you can find (sample as many as convenient)?
5. Any other tabs worth knowing about for a people/CRM schema (e.g. a household/family tab, a manual-notes tab, a merge/dedup tracking tab)?

This is investigation only — do not modify anything, don't call Artifact or other write tools. Report back concisely (under 500 words): tab list, header drift findings, sample-row evidence of contact-info drift across registrations, and whether any change-history mechanism already exists. Quote real data sparingly (a couple of example rows is enough, no need to dump everything).

input.new_string:
**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.

| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                     | primary key                                    |
| `name`              | string                   |                                                 |
| `category`          | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
| `clubspot_camp_id`  | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                              |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
"Advanced"). Modeled now, not deferred: a registration is for a specific session *and* class, and
#70's sync needs somewhere to put that — see `registrations` below.

| Field                | Type                      | Notes             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                  | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`          | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
| `name`                | string                   |                   |
| `clubspot_class_id`   | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

Not modeled: which classes a given session offers (Clubspot's `CampSession.campClassesArray`) or
per-class/session capacity (`EntryCap`) — that's capacity-planning territory for the
financial-model-replacement app, not something the people hub's roster/permission needs require.

**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
the financial model.

| Field                       | Type                                        | Notes                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                        | uuid                                        | primary key                                                 |
| `person_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                             |
| `session_id`                | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                              |
| `class_id`                  | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                              |
| `status`                    | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the *current* status — see [Change tracking](#change-tracking) for history |
| `clubspot_registration_id`  | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone** |
| `clubspot_session_join_id`  | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id) |

### Change tracking

Registration status isn't a fact that just happens once — a row moves waitlist → confirmed →
cancelled, and knowing *when* matters (for reporting, and because Clubspot itself already tracks
it: `RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates` is a timestamped array of status changes on their
side). A flat `status` column loses that the moment #70 overwrites it. So:

- **`registration_status_events`** — append-only, one row per status transition.

  | Field               | Type                                         | Notes                                             |
  | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                | uuid                                         | primary key                                       |
  | `registration_id`   | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`               |                                                    |
  | `status`            | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`)  |                                                    |
  | `changed_at`        | timestamp                                    | when the status actually changed, per Clubspot's own `waitlist_updates`/`confirmed_at` |
  | `recorded_at`       | timestamp, default now()                     | when #70's sync wrote this row (may lag `changed_at` if sync polls infrequently) |

  #70 should backfill this from Clubspot's own history (`waitlist_updates`, `confirmed_at`) rather
  than only logging transitions it happens to observe between polls — Clubspot already did the hard
  part. `registrations.status` stays as the current-value cache every other collection joins
  against; this table is where the history lives.

### Data provenance

People data is an aggregation, not a source: `people.email`/`phone` are collected from whatever a
registration's contact form said, and the same real person can supply different values on different
registrations (a guardian re-registers a second child two years later with a new email address).
Confirmed by looking at the actual participants spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace): it's a
fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with **no timestamp or version on any row today** — there's
nothing to tell a conflicting value apart from a stale one, or to say which registration a person's
current email came from.

- **`person_field_history`** — append-only, one row per observed value.

  | Field                    | Type                                              | Notes                                  |
  | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                     | uuid                                              | primary key                            |
  | `person_id`              | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                          |                                         |
  | `field`                  | enum (`email`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`) | which `people` field this observation is for |
  | `value`                  | string                                            |                                         |
  | `source_registration_id` | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`, nullable          | null if a staff member entered/corrected it directly in Directus instead |
  | `observed_at`            | timestamp                                        | the registration's own date — when this value was actually submitted |
  | `recorded_at`            | timestamp, default now()                          | when #70's sync wrote this row |

  `people.email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` stay as the current-value cache (#70 updates them
  to whichever source has the latest `observed_at`); this table is the audit trail behind them, and
  what a staff member would open to resolve "which of these two emails on file is right."

  Considered one polymorphic history table shared between this and `registration_status_events`
  (same shape: value + source + timestamps) — kept them separate instead. Two small, plainly-typed
  tables are easier to write permission filters against (e.g. a Guardian's own-minor scope) than one
  generic table needing a many-to-any relation to know what it's a history *of*.

3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  programs/sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a
15	  household, only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys
16	  off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **registration** (`Registration`) — not "enrollment." Clubspot's **class**
19	  (`CampClass`) concept is named for, but not modeled by, this schema — see the `programs`/`sessions`
20	  note below.
21	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
22	  below.
23	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
24	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
25	
26	### Collections
27	
28	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
29	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
30	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
31	participant from a `registrations` row.
32	
33	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
34	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
35	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
36	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
37	
38	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
39	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
40	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
41	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
42	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
43	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
44	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
45	
46	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
47	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
48	contact).
49	
50	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
51	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
52	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
53	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
54	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
55	
56	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
57	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
58	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
59	one's `relationship_type` enum.
60	
61	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
62	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
63	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
64	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
65	fields into rows here.
66	
67	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
68	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
69	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
70	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
71	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
72	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
73	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
74	
75	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
76	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
77	[Permission model](#permission-model).
78	
79	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
80	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
81	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
82	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
83	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
84	
85	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
86	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
87	
88	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                          |
89	| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
90	| `id`                | uuid                     | primary key                                    |
91	| `name`              | string                   |                                                 |
92	| `category`          | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
93	| `clubspot_camp_id`  | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                              |
94	
95	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
96	
97	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
98	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
99	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
100	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
101	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
102	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
103	
104	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
105	"Advanced"). Modeled now, not deferred: a registration is for a specific session *and* class, and
106	#70's sync needs somewhere to put that — see `registrations` below.
107	
108	| Field                | Type                      | Notes             |
109	| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
110	| `id`                  | uuid                      | primary key       |
111	| `program_id`          | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
112	| `name`                | string                   |                   |
113	| `clubspot_class_id`   | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |
114	
115	Not modeled: which classes a given session offers (Clubspot's `CampSession.campClassesArray`) or
116	per-class/session capacity (`EntryCap`) — that's capacity-planning territory for the
117	financial-model-replacement app, not something the people hub's roster/permission needs require.
118	
119	**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
120	matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
121	`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
122	its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
123	becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
124	does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
125	the financial model.
126	
127	| Field                       | Type                                        | Notes                                                       |
128	| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
129	| `id`                        | uuid                                        | primary key                                                 |
130	| `person_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                             |
131	| `session_id`                | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                              |
132	| `class_id`                  | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                              |
133	| `status`                    | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the *current* status — see [Change tracking](#change-tracking) for history |
134	| `clubspot_registration_id`  | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone** |
135	| `clubspot_session_join_id`  | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id) |
136	
137	### Change tracking
138	
139	Registration status isn't a fact that just happens once — a row moves waitlist → confirmed →
140	cancelled, and knowing *when* matters (for reporting, and because Clubspot itself already tracks
141	it: `RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates` is a timestamped array of status changes on their
142	side). A flat `status` column loses that the moment #70 overwrites it. So:
143	
144	- **`registration_status_events`** — append-only, one row per status transition.
145	
146	  | Field               | Type                                         | Notes                                             |
147	  | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
148	  | `id`                | uuid                                         | primary key                                       |
149	  | `registration_id`   | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`               |                                                    |
150	  | `status`            | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`)  |                                                    |
151	  | `changed_at`        | timestamp                                    | when the status actually changed, per Clubspot's own `waitlist_updates`/`confirmed_at` |
152	  | `recorded_at`       | timestamp, default now()                     | when #70's sync wrote this row (may lag `changed_at` if sync polls infrequently) |
153	
154	  #70 should backfill this from Clubspot's own history (`waitlist_updates`, `confirmed_at`) rather
155	  than only logging transitions it happens to observe between polls — Clubspot already did the hard
156	  part. `registrations.status` stays as the current-value cache every other collection joins
157	  against; this table is where the history lives.
158	
159	### Data provenance
160	
161	People data is an aggregation, not a source: `people.email`/`phone` are collected from whatever a
162	registration's contact form said, and the same real person can supply different values on different
163	registrations (a guardian re-registers a second child two years later with a new email address).
164	Confirmed by looking at the actual participants spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace): it's a
165	fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with **no timestamp or version on any row today** — there's
166	nothing to tell a conflicting value apart from a stale one, or to say which registration a person's
167	current email came from.
168	
169	- **`person_field_history`** — append-only, one row per observed value.
170	
171	  | Field                    | Type                                              | Notes                                  |
172	  | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
173	  | `id`                     | uuid                                              | primary key                            |
174	  | `person_id`              | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                          |                                         |
175	  | `field`                  | enum (`email`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`) | which `people` field this observation is for |
176	  | `value`                  | string                                            |                                         |
177	  | `source_registration_id` | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`, nullable          | null if a staff member entered/corrected it directly in Directus instead |
178	  | `observed_at`            | timestamp                                        | the registration's own date — when this value was actually submitted |
179	  | `recorded_at`            | timestamp, default now()                          | when #70's sync wrote this row |
180	
181	  `people.email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` stay as the current-value cache (#70 updates them
182	  to whichever source has the latest `observed_at`); this table is the audit trail behind them, and
183	  what a staff member would open to resolve "which of these two emails on file is right."
184	
185	  Considered one polymorphic history table shared between this and `registration_status_events`
186	  (same shape: value + source + timestamps) — kept them separate instead. Two small, plainly-typed
187	  tables are easier to write permission filters against (e.g. a Guardian's own-minor scope) than one
188	  generic table needing a many-to-any relation to know what it's a history *of*.
189	
190	### Auth identity
191	
192	Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
193	— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
194	Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:
195	
196	- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
197	  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
198	  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
199	- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
200	  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
201	  at the resulting user once one exists.
202	
203	### Permission model
204	
205	- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
206	- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
207	  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
208	  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
209	- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
210	  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` / `registrations` /
211	  `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only their own sessions via
212	  `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
213	- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
214	  `medical_profiles` / `registrations`, filtered through `contacts` where
215	  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
216	  — it's the medical-data boundary the whole design doc exists to get right.
217	- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
218	  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.
219	
220	### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)
221	
222	- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) for every collection above — pick
223	  whichever keeps the permission filters simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
224	- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
225	  Guardian role ever actually logs in.
226	- The actual person-dedup rule #70 will use (email match, most likely, with a manual merge path for
227	  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.
228

Pushed the update and posted a summary on PR #96. To recap what changed based on your latest comment and request:

- **Modeled `classes` now** (not deferred) — added the collection and moved `registrations` down to Clubspot's actual finest grain (session + class, matching `RegistrationCampSession`/"Session Join Id" in the existing sync report), rather than the coarser session-only row I had before.
- **Change tracking**: added `registration_status_events`, sourced from Clubspot's own `waitlist_updates` history rather than reinventing it from scratch.
- **Data provenance**: added `person_field_history` to track which registration supplied a given email/phone/name and when — confirmed by pulling the live participants spreadsheet that today's sync has zero timestamp/versioning, so there's genuinely nothing distinguishing a stale value from a real conflict right now.

CI is running on the new commit — I'll let you know when it's green.
